newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH BOND PRICES REVIVE ON U.S. GAINS.
newsitem.headline: DANISH BOND PRICES REVIVE ON U.S. GAINS.

text.p: Danish bond prices rallied on Thursday morning, pulled up Wednesday's closing gains on the U.S. treasury market.
"It looks as if we found a floor on Wednesday, therefore there is hope for a more positive market (today) a dealer said.
Shortly after opening, the Danish benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.55, yielding 6.06 percent, up 0.30 point from Wednesday's close.
The seven percent 2007 paper, due to become the benchmark on September 1, was up 0.34 point to 105.44, yielding 6.25 percent.
The 2007's yield spread to the German 10-year bund widened two basis points to 59 bp.
